🔍 Data quality, diversity and fleets

Source: vignettes/articles/quality-diversity-fleets.Rmd
quality-diversity-fleets.Rmd
📦 Data: FAO Global Capture Production, release 2026.1.0 (published by FAO on 2026-03-30; catches 1950–2024), downloaded from Capture_2026.1.0.zip. Licence CC BY 4.0. fao_data_info() shows the release you use and how to cite it.

Like the analyses of 📈 Composition, stock status and trends, these functions take any catch data: a fishing area from fishing_area_data(), or any subset of load_fao_data(). Their charts are saved in figures/png/summary/ and their tables in tables/, with the name of the area at the start of the file names (or label), and they return their results invisibly.

FAO27 <- fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Northeast")

⚙️ Common arguments

All four functions have these arguments; the tables of each function list only its own.

Argument Meaning Default
area_data FAO catch data: fishing_area_data()$area_data, or any subset of load_fao_data() (e.g. one country, or several fishing areas) required
plot Save the charts in figures/png/summary/ TRUE
table Save the tables in tables/ TRUE
lang Language of the chart text and names: "en", "zh" or "both" NULL: the language of fao_settings() ("en" unless changed)
pptx Also save the charts as editable PowerPoint files in figures/pptx/summary/ FALSE; fao_settings(pptx = TRUE) changes it for all functions
label Name at the start of the output file names NULL: the fishing area of the data (or its country; "selected_data" for several areas and countries)

🧪 Data quality

data_quality() shows two aspects of the statistics over time:

  • the share of the catch reported officially (FAO status flag A), the share estimated by the country or imputed by FAO (flags E and I), and the share with other flags (e.g. provisional or negligible values);
  • the share of the catch identified to species, genus, family, or only to an order or a higher group such as “Marine fishes nei”, from the FAO taxonomic codes.
quality <- data_quality(FAO27$area_data)

A large estimated share in the latest years usually means that FAO has not yet received the national reports; these values are often revised in the next release (Garibaldi 2012). The country table shows, for the countries with the largest catch in the last five years, how much of their catch in those years was estimated and how much identified to species:

show_table(quality$countries, digits = 1)
country country_en catch_last_5_years estimated_pct species_level_pct

Iceland Iceland 6329277 0.0 99.4
Russian Federation Russian Federation 4811200 0.0 99.6
United Kingdom United Kingdom 3340084 0.0 96.9
Faroe Islands Faroe Islands 3252896 0.0 98.1
Denmark Denmark 2606338 0.0 79.8
France France 1824629 0.2 91.0
Netherlands (Kingdom of the) Netherlands (Kingdom of the) 1327367 0.0 100.0
Spain Spain 1271825 0.0 94.4
Ireland Ireland 1142570 16.4 85.8
Argument Meaning Default
top_n Number of countries in the country table 10
area_data, plot, table, lang, pptx, label See Common arguments

Output: <label>_data_quality_status_share.png and <label>_data_quality_taxon_share.png, and the tables <label>_data_quality_status.csv, ..._taxon.csv and ..._countries.csv; the function returns data_status, taxon_level (yearly catch by category) and countries.

The FAO statistics are the catches reported by countries (and estimated by FAO when no report arrives). Catch reconstructions that add estimates of unreported catches and discards found global marine catches higher than reported, and declining more strongly since their peak (Pauly and Zeller 2016). The data quality charts show how the reported statistics were made, not how complete they are.

🌈 Diversity and concentration

diversity_concentration() computes, for each year:

Indicator Column Calculation
Number of species reported n_species Items identified to species with catch
Number of countries n_countries Countries with catch
Shannon diversity (Shannon 1948) shannon_species H=−∑ipiln⁡piH = -\sum_i p_i \ln p_i, with pip_i the share of species item ii (all items, including “nei” groups) in the year’s catch
HHI of species / countries (Rhoades 1993) hhi_species, hhi_countries HHI=∑i(100pi)2\text{HHI} = \sum_i (100\,p_i)^2, from 0 to 10 000
Top-N share top5_species_pct, top5_countries_pct Share (%) of the top_n largest species items or countries (the column names follow top_n) 
diversity <- diversity_concentration(FAO27$area_data, top_n = 5)
show_table(subset(diversity, Year %in% c(1970, 1990, 2010, max(Year))), digits = 2)
Year n_species n_countries shannon_species hhi_species hhi_countries top5_species_pct top5_countries_pct
1970 1970 107 22 3.02 897.68 1,348.67 60.29 71.05
1990 1990 161 24 3.32 631.00 1,199.47 48.53 68.73
2010 2010 280 26 3.21 862.25 1,405.73 53.74 69.11
2024 2024 514 32 2.96 1,100.44 1,226.80 64.95 67.81
Argument Meaning Default
top_n Number of largest species items and countries in the top share 5
area_data, plot, table, lang, pptx, label See Common arguments

Output: <label>_diversity.png (all indicators) and the table <label>_diversity.csv; the function returns a data frame with one row per year.

Reading the indicators. A higher Shannon index means more species items and a more even catch; its maximum is ln⁡S\ln S for SS items. In the US merger guidelines (U.S. Department of Justice and Federal Trade Commission 2010), an HHI below 1 500 is unconcentrated, 1 500 to 2 500 moderately and above 2 500 highly concentrated. For example, three species with shares of 50%, 30% and 20% give H=1.03H = 1.03 and HHI=502+302+202=3800\text{HHI} = 50^2 + 30^2 + 20^2 = 3\,800.

The indicators use FAO species items, including “nei” groups. When FAO splits a “nei” group into species, Shannon diversity rises and HHI falls even if nothing changed at sea. Country indicators change when countries split, e.g. the USSR in 1991.

🏳️ Country groups

country_group_summary() sums the catch by groups of countries from the FAO country list: World Bank income group, continent or region. It saves a chart of the catch of each group and one of its share, and a table by decade like that of species_group_composition().

income <- country_group_summary(FAO27$area_data, group = "income")
country_group_summary(FAO27$area_data, group = "region", top_n = 6, lang = "zh")
Argument Meaning Default
group "income" (World Bank income groups), "continent" or "region" "income"
top_n Number of groups shown separately; the others are combined 8
area_data, plot, table, lang, pptx, label See Common arguments

Output: <label>_country_income.png (or _continent, _region) and ..._share.png, and the table <label>_country_income.csv; the function returns yearly and table.

🚢 Coastal countries and distant-water fleets

coastal_distant() splits the catch between countries that border the fishing area and distant-water fleets from elsewhere, and shows the main distant-water countries.

A country is coastal to an area if its land (including overseas territories, from the Natural Earth map units) lies within 20 km of the FAO area boundary (the FAO major fishing areas of the CWP handbook). Former countries such as the USSR take the coastline of their successor states. In area 34 (Eastern Central Atlantic), for example, Spain and Portugal count as coastal because of the Canary Islands and Madeira. Catch reported as “Other nei” is shown as unknown.

fleets <- coastal_distant(FAO27$area_data)
show_table(fleets$table, digits = 0)
Fleet 1950s 1960s 1970s 1980s 1990s 2000s 2010s 2020s 2020 2021 2022 2023 2024 share_2024_pct
Coastal countries 6,956,166 8,930,049 11,522,278 10,722,687 10,713,646 10,080,097 8,899,457 8,445,147 8,598,826 8,343,100 8,719,874 8,738,529 7,825,406 100
Distant-water countries 0 1,000 20,186 14,021 16,346 3,569 7,511 12,742 10,649 15,624 9,353 11,298 16,787 0
Unknown 0 0 0 2 107 0 1,144 930 2,227 2 2,420 2 2 0
Argument Meaning Default
top_n Number of distant-water countries shown separately 8
area_data, plot, table, lang, pptx, label See Common arguments

The analysis works for marine areas; inland areas in the data are left out with a message. Output: <label>_coastal_distant.png and ..._share.png (coastal, distant-water and unknown catch), <label>_coastal_distant_countries.png (main distant-water countries), and the tables <label>_coastal_distant.csv and ..._countries.csv; the function returns yearly, distant and table. The profiles of the main distant-water countries are in 🔬 Shocks, collapses, synchrony and fleets.

📝 In the Word report

fao_report() writes data quality, diversity and concentration, and coastal and distant-water fleets into the Word report of a fishing area (see 📝 Assessment report: Word, LaTeX and PDF): they are the sections quality, diversity and fleets, all on by default. Their settings are given with the section name as prefix (quality_ for data_quality(), diversity_ for diversity_concentration(), fleets_ for coastal_distant()), and a section is left out with FALSE:

fao_report(27, diversity_top_n = 3, fleets = FALSE)

country_group_summary() is not part of the report.
